posts.body:
Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf just declared the era of "proportionate responses" over, promising a "faster, heavier, and more painful" answer to U.S. attacks. This comes after CENTCOM struck three Iranian crude carriers in response to Revolutionary Guard missiles fired at two U.S. Navy warships. When bombs hit tankers, oil traders don't wait for the press conference — they front-run the headline.

Here's the part most people miss: Ghalibaf also admitted Iran is buckling under inflation, unemployment, and exchange-rate chaos. That's the real signal. A regime escalating militarily while its economy craters is the exact setup where every new headline swings Brent and WTI by dollars, not cents. Geopolitical risk isn't background noise anymore — it's the primary catalyst.

This is precisely the kind of binary, headline-driven event that prediction markets were built to price. Will there be another tanker strike this month? Does Brent close above a key level before the next round? On EventTrader you can take a position on the escalation itself instead of guessing which oil major benefits. Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/06/iran-us-response-oil-tanker-strikes.html

Volatility is opportunity — but only if you're positioned before the next Telegram post from Tehran, not after.
posts.title: Iran Warns of 'More Painful' Strikes — The War Premium Is Back in Oil

posts.body:
Chilean exchange **Orionx** — backed by Tether in a 2025 Series A — is winding down after a forensic audit found more than **$7M in customer assets** had walked out to wallets it didn't control. Withdrawals are frozen, a criminal complaint is filed against two co-founders, and the alleged transfers reportedly trace back to **2018–2021** across BTC, ETH, XRP, and POL. ([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/orionx-shut-down-7-million-move-outside-wallets))

The brutal lesson: *if you can't verify it on-chain, you don't own it.* Orionx's own systems showed balances that reality didn't back — a gap that sat undetected for years until the numbers were compared against verifiable on-chain data. That's the entire case for exchanges where reserves are provable and settlement produces a real tx hash you can inspect yourself.

For traders, this is a tradeable narrative, not just a headline. "Which CEX survives the next audit?" is exactly the kind of question prediction markets exist to price. Custody-risk premiums, insurer flows, and the slow rotation toward provable-reserve venues are the real story underneath a single $7M hole — and the smart position is built on data you can check, not balances someone else typed into a database.
posts.title: $7M Vanished From a Tether-Backed Exchange — This Is Why Custody Is a Bet
